references.text: Lot shows similar hospitality to Abraham by insisting on welcoming the guests and baking unleavened bread (ugot) for them – a direct parallel to Abraham's cakes.
Gideon prepares food including unleavened bread for the angel of the Lord, a close parallel to Abraham's preparation of cakes for his divine guests.
The woman at En-Dor hurried to prepare food with dough and unleavened bread for Saul, following a similar pattern of quick preparation.
Martha welcomes Jesus into her home and is busy serving the guests, an act of hospitality that can be compared to Abraham's and Sarah's busy preparations.
The exhortation to show hospitality to strangers – some have without knowing it entertained angels – is a clear reference to Abraham's experience in Gen 18.
Abraham's concrete hospitality in Genesis is the historical model for Paul's theological call to hospitality in Romans.
